target.title: fix(line): cap message action text length
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

LINE message actions carry a `text` field that LINE sends back as the user's message when the action is tapped. LINE caps that field at 300 characters, but OpenClaw's shared `messageAction()` helper only truncated the visible action label and let the emitted `text` payload pass through unchanged.

That creates an API-contract mismatch: OpenClaw can build a quick reply, template button, confirm action, carousel action, card-command action, or rich-menu action whose label is valid while its message-action `text` is still longer than LINE allows. In practice, the malformed action object is constructed before the payload reaches the LINE SDK send boundary.

The narrow pre-fix trigger was:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 301
```

The affected user-realistic path is:

```text
quick replies / template buttons / confirm actions / carousel actions / card commands / rich menus
  -> messageAction(label, text)
  -> LINE SDK payload
  -> LINE Messaging API
```

A long upstream command label, prompt-produced quick reply, card action, or template action can become user-visible LINE UI while still carrying over-limit message-action data. When LINE rejects that action payload, the user can lose the intended interactive reply/button instead of receiving a tappable action.

## Why This Change Was Made

The production change stays at the shared action-constructor boundary, but now uses a LINE message-action-specific grapheme cap instead of the UTF-16 action-data cap used by postback and datetime picker data:

```diff
 export function messageAction(label: string, text?: string): Action {
   return {
     type: "message",
     label: truncateLineActionLabel(label),
-    text: text ?? label,
+    text: truncateLineMessageText(text ?? label),
   };
 }
```

This keeps the fix centralized for all `messageAction()` callers while matching LINE's message-action text counting contract. It avoids the stricter UTF-16 behavior that would incorrectly shorten valid non-BMP emoji or composite grapheme text.

Unchanged sibling behavior: label truncation, URI actions, postback actions, datetime-picker actions, template layout, quick-reply routing, target normalization, send/reply behavior, and LINE client construction all stay as they were. Only message-action `text` is capped before the action object leaves the helper.

## User Impact

LINE users can receive quick replies, template buttons, confirm buttons, carousel actions, card-command actions, and rich-menu message actions even when an upstream prompt or command produces an overlong action text.

Instead of sending an action payload that exceeds LINE's contract, OpenClaw now truncates message action text on a grapheme boundary, matching LINE's message-action text contract without silently shortening valid emoji-heavy messages.

## Compatibility Behavior

This PR intentionally chooses LINE-contract truncation instead of preserving an over-limit action payload that LINE rejects. For any current or future caller that passes more than 300 grapheme clusters to `messageAction(label, text)`, OpenClaw now emits the first 300 grapheme clusters as the LINE message-action `text`.

That means a user tapping an over-limit quick reply, template action, card command, or rich-menu message action sends the truncated command text instead of losing the interactive action to a LINE API validation failure. The previous payload was already outside LINE's accepted contract, so this change turns a non-deliverable action into a deliverable, contract-compliant one.

If maintainers prefer a different channel-wide overflow policy, such as surfacing an upstream error or replacing long structured commands with postback/mapped command IDs, this PR should pause for that design decision. Otherwise, the intended compatibility behavior is centralized truncation at the shared `messageAction()` boundary, with URI, postback, datetime-picker, routing, target normalization, and SDK client behavior left unchanged.

## Evidence

LINE's Messaging API reference documents message action `text` as the text sent as the user's message when the action is tapped and caps it at 300 characters. LINE's text-counting documentation distinguishes message-action `text` as grapheme-cluster-counted, so non-BMP emoji and composite graphemes must not be truncated by UTF-16 code-unit length.

References:

- https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#message-action
- https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/text-character-count/

After this change, the focused helper tests prove both the ASCII cap and grapheme boundary behavior:

```ts
messageAction("Go", "x".repeat(301)).text.length === 300
messageAction("Go", "\u{1f600}".repeat(300)).text === "\u{1f600}".repeat(300)
messageAction("Go", "e\u0301".repeat(301)).text === "e\u0301".repeat(300)
```

After-fix outbound-path proof was added at the LINE SDK boundary. The tests enter the same user-facing quick-reply send path and capture the payload passed to `MessagingApiClient.pushMessage()`:

```text
pushTextMessageWithQuickReplies("line:user:U123", "Pick one", ["x".repeat(301)], ...)
  -> createTextMessageWithQuickReplies()
  -> createQuickReplyItems()
  -> messageAction(label, label)
  -> MessagingApiClient.pushMessage({ messages: [{ quickReply: ... }] })
```

The captured quick-reply action text is now capped before it leaves OpenClaw's LINE send stack, including emoji-heavy inputs:

```ts
expect(quickReplyItem.action?.text).toHaveLength(300)
expect(graphemeLength(emojiQuickReply.action.text)).toBe(300)
```

Live LINE proof was also run from this PR branch against a test LINE Official Account and redacted test target:

```text
source: OpenClaw current PR branch messageAction() -> LINE validate/push
ASCII input action text: 301 UTF-16 code units
API-facing ASCII action text after fix: 300 UTF-16 code units
output ends with dangling high surrogate: false
target: U9f...9c94
validate endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push
validate response: HTTP 200 {}, x-line-request-id e15daf14-5890-4b6b-ad5f-ef56fadb1588
push endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/push
push response: HTTP 200, x-line-request-id 9501fe3e-5962-44ad-af12-a50c30866d74
sent message id: 623300370231197926
```

A second real LINE validate run covered the reviewer-requested grapheme boundary without sending another user message:

```text
source: OpenClaw current PR branch messageAction() -> LINE validate/push
emoji input action text: 301 graphemes
API-facing emoji action text after fix: 300 graphemes
API-facing emoji action text after fix: 600 UTF-16 code units
preserves 300 emoji: true
validate endpoint: POST /v2/bot/message/validate/push
validate response: HTTP 200 {}, x-line-request-id 9dfecf5c-a1a7-4424-86ff-5325881114cf
```

Terminal capture:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/send.test.ts -t "sends quick reply action text within LINE's 300 grapheme limit"

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  1 passed | 23 skipped (24)
```

Validation:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/rich-menu.test.ts extensions/line/src/message-cards.test.ts extensions/line/src/reply-payload-transform.test.ts extensions/line/src/send.test.ts` - passed, 104 tests
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/line/src/rich-menu.test.ts extensions/line/src/send.test.ts` - passed, 44 tests
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/actions.ts extensions/line/src/rich-menu.test.ts extensions/line/src/send.test.ts` - passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions` - passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` - passed
- `git diff --check` - passed

No access token, full user ID, channel secret, private chat content, or full quote token is included in this PR evidence. The proof token was used only for this test and should be rotated after proof capture.
